To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
quality assurance is an important part of high volume document digitisation projects and that there are several methods to achieve quality control.

quality bottlenecks exist throughout the whole processing chain of document image processing, that the quality of the final output is highly affected by the quality of the input data, and that the quality of input data is highly affected by human factors such as training and user interface design.

the quality bottlenecks in high volume document image processing are the lack of ground truth data, the difficulty of evaluating recognition performance, the lack of effective quality metrics and the lack of effective QA methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quality of digitized documents.

the following issues: (1) what are the major quality bottlenecks throughout the processing pipeline, and how they can be addressed; (2) how to conduct cost-effective quality assurance in high volume digitization projects, and how to design a user interface to make the QA process more efficient.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
QA should be a continuous and iterative process, with auto-QA and human QA being combined in different phases of the processing pipeline.
the QA in high volume document projects should be a combination of auto-QAs and manual QA, with the latter being the final QA, which is also called the “gold standard”.

there is no one-size-fit-all QA strategy, but the most effective QA is a combination of auto-QAs, batch QA, and manual QA, and the most cost-effective QA is a combination that fits the specific digitization project.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
QA in document digitization is a complex and challenging task.
QA should be a systematic, iterative process, and it is critical to have an overall QA strategy to ensure quality and to reduce cost.
QA is a complex issue and there are no universal solutions, but there is a set of best practices that can be followed in most cases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
QA should not be considered an isolated task but as an integral part of document digitization.
QA in high volume digitization projects should be conducted in an end-to-end fashion.
the quality of the digitized document is determined by a combination of the quality of the input documents, the processing pipeline, and the QA system.
